title: The Sum of Subarray Ranges

concept.title: Sum of maximums minus sum of minimums, each by counting
body: The **range** of a subarray is `max - min`. The sum of the ranges over all subarrays is the **sum of all maximums** minus the **sum of all minimums**, and the two sums are found in the same way. Do not look at the subarrays. Look at the elements: how many subarrays have `a[j]` as their maximum? A subarray has `a[j]` as maximum if it starts after the nearest greater-or-equal element on the left (position `L`) and ends before the nearest strictly greater element on the right (position `R`): `(j - L)` choices for the start and `(R - j)` choices for the end. (The unequal treatment of equal values makes sure that a subarray with several equal maximums is counted once.)

A monotonic stack finds `L` and `R` in one pass: when `a[i]` is greater than the top element `a[j]`, then `i` is the nearest strictly greater element to the right of `j`, and the element below `j` on the stack is its nearest greater-or-equal element on the left.
The sum is large (up to about `4 * 10^17`), so use 64-bit integers in C++ and Java.

statement: For an array of `n` numbers, the range of a subarray is its largest element minus its smallest element. Print the sum of the ranges of all contiguous subarrays.
hints: The sum of ranges is the sum of the maximums minus the sum of the minimums.
For each element count the subarrays in which it is the maximum, using the nearest greater element on each side.
Break ties between equal values in one direction to avoid counting a subarray twice; get the minimums from the negated array.

explanation: A monotonic stack gives, for every element, how many subarrays have it as the maximum; the same on the negated array gives the minimums. The answer is the sum of the maximums minus the sum of the minimums.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def sum_of_maximums(a):
    total = 0
    stack = []
    for i in range(len(a) + 1):
        while stack and (i == len(a) or a[stack[-1]] < a[i]):
            j = stack.pop()
            left = stack[-1] if stack else -1
            total += a[j] * (j - left) * (i - j)
        stack.append(i)
    return total

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

print(sum_of_maximums(a) + sum_of_maximums([-x for x in a]))
